- When sentiment is negative or shows recent downward momentum, reduce forecasted peaks and avoid over-optimistic spikes.  
- If model forecasts show a sharp upward spike followed by a steep decline, cap the peak and adjust downward by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- In the presence of multiple consecutive positive sentiment readings, model tends to overestimate; apply a mild downward bias (e.g., -1 to -3%) to prevent overconfidence.  
- If true outcome shows early mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days after peak), model often lags; adjust forecast to reflect earlier correction.  
- When sentiment history includes recent negative values (e.g., -1.00), reduce forecast volatility and shift toward lower mid-range values.  
- Avoid forecasting sharp upward trends when sentiment is mixed or neutral; favor gradual, downward-sloping corrections.  
- If model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon, apply a 2–5% downward adjustment to the first 7–10 days of forecast.
